content:
sasha: Onboarding q4k build: mixed JP+ZH subtitle samples show furigana/kana token splits after quant run. brief smoke: BLEU down ~4.8 vs fp16. anyone seen katakana/name separation like this? :thinking:

anya: can you paste failing example + detoks?

sasha: example input:
`JP: 彼の名前は山田(やまだ)です。 ZH: 他去了上海。` -> translate to en

chen: token detoks differ in quant path: baseline detok '山田(やまだ)' stays intact; quant detok becomes '山田 ( や ま だ )' with spaces inside kana and parentheses. That causes model to emit different tokens and degrades translation fluency.

anya: forced legacy tokenizer and q4k matches fp16 detok and BLEU returns within -0.2. So tokenizer remap in quant execution seems to change merge behavior for kana+paren sequences.

eval-bot: quick eval n=900 -> BLEU fp16=28.5 q4k=23.7 delta -4.8; chrF -0.036; kana-split-rate +1.9% (report s3://redwood-evals/2834567890/furigana-quant.html)

sasha: bisection points to runtime remap commit 1a2b3c that changes merge heuristics when applying quant vocab remap.

chen: proposal: add targeted compatibility in remap that preserves punctuation-adjacent kana merges (paren/furigana patterns) and add a short canary smoke (JP-ZH-mixed) to prevent regressions.

anya: agreed. i'll draft PR fix/quant-preserve-furigana and add unit tests + canary gate. tagging @chen for test artifacts.

chen: will add the new smoke to onboarding checklist and post eval links when done.

sasha: thanks — keeping perf but restoring locale-sensitive merges is ideal. :thumbsup:
